rows.practice_entry: 22. A kill that attributes to nothing is a pass — the same output, two diseases, on the other side
rows.notes: This IS the mutation engine (8,690 lines): manifest-driven mutations, kill attribution by parsing each guard's --self-test output, the cost-balanced shard partition (sweep_shard / sweep_partition) and the import-closure selection (select_manifests). Spec 2c reads C3 against GitHub Actions plus an ARBITRARY mutation engine, so shipping this engine as the CI layer's dependency is the C3 failure the spec names; the plan expects DON'T-SHIP with a practice harvest. C3 fail, argued from the scan: check-plan-code:4:1 and :4:2 are guard-name self-paths (lines 8162, 8165), :6:1 reads PC495_STATE (a variable this repo defines), :2:1 is one of ten unread repo paths; HARNESS_TREE names this repo's directories (scripts, supabase, docs, node_modules/typescript). C2 pass, argued: :6:3 reads GITHUB_ACTIONS, which GitHub Actions provides, and no Supabase/Gemini/Fly edge was emitted. C4 fail, argued: every mutation is a hand-written manifest anchored to one of THIS repo's guards, so a stranger's repository has nothing for it to mutate. Practice harvest: section 22 (kill attribution through parsed output) exists; section 10 (a surviving mutation first asks whether the guard can fire) is a second candidate. Practices with NO heading yet (left for Task 20, not claimed here): cost-balanced sharding with a loud round-robin fallback; selecting suites by import closure. Costs: public bar = make it engine-agnostic (a manifest format any repo can author, no repo-path constants, a documented record schema); next project = copy it and re-anchor manifests to that project's guards.

Pieces (a) matrix sharding and (c) the scheduled full sweep live here: the mutation-sweep job (.github/workflows/ci.yml line 1117) is a 38-shard matrix (max-parallel 12 on the schedule), the nightly cron is '30 8 * * *', and the mutation-sweep-complete step runs scripts/sweep-red-alert.py. C3 fail, argued from the scan's cwd-relative findings: :2:98 (check-plan-code --self-test, line 1024), :2:107 (check-plan-code --mutate, line 1515), :2:108 (sweep-red-alert.py, line 1628) and :2:21 (fixture_git, line 471) call this repo's scripts by repo-relative path; a `uses:` caller's checkout has none of them. C2 pass, argued: the sweep steps need only GitHub Actions, Python and git. C4 fail, argued (spec 2c: C4 stays argued, no experiment): there is no reusable-workflow file to put on a `uses:` line yet. Bound: this component is the WHOLE ci.yml, so 104 of its 108 scan findings are outside-set paths of OTHER jobs' steps and do not bear on the sweep. Route: extract the job into a reusable workflow with `on: workflow_call` whose inputs name the caller's mutation command, shard count and schedule-driven budget; the engine becomes an input, which is what spec 2c's C3 asks. harvest none: no portable-practices heading covers sharding or the scheduled sweep (a candidate for Task 20). Engine comparison for pieces (a) and (c): the top-level engine_comparison list.

Piece (c)'s alert: reads every shard's record and opens or comments on a `sweep-red` (and `sweep-flaky`) issue, never closing one. C3 fail, argued: sweep-red-alert:4:1 is its importlib load of check-plan-code.py, and it requires RECORD_SCHEMA to equal check-plan-code's (check-plan-code.py line 2988), so it reads our engine's record format; it also imports coverage_verdict. C2 pass, argued: sweep-red-alert:6:1 is the git executable, which a GitHub runner has; issues go through the Actions token. Route: ship inside the same reusable workflow, reading a documented record schema that any engine's wrapper can write, instead of loading our engine. harvest none: no heading for the scheduled-sweep alert pattern exists.

engine_comparison.scope: plan Task 17: pieces (a) matrix sharding, (b) selection by closure / observed reach, (c) scheduled full sweep with a sweep-red issue, against the incremental and shard modes of Stryker, mutmut, PIT and cargo-mutants, from each project's own documentation fetched 2026-11-22. 'Not documented' means not found IN THE PAGES LISTED, not that the engine lacks it.

ours.a: check-plan-code.py sweep_shard / sweep_partition: N shards of equal ESTIMATED cost from scripts/sweep-costs.json, round-robin when no costs table; ci.yml mutation-sweep matrix of 38 shards.
ours.b: check-plan-code.py select_manifests: on a PR, selects the guard SUITES (manifests) whose import closure the diff reaches; observed-reach selection (backlog #586, strace) is in progress and not in the components map.
ours.c: ci.yml cron '30 8 * * *' runs the full sweep; sweep-red-alert.py opens or comments on a sweep-red issue.

rows.capability: Parallelism is a `concurrency` count of worker processes on one machine; sharding one run across CI jobs is not documented in the fetched pages.
Runs mutants in parallel worker processes on one machine; sharding across jobs is not documented in the fetched pages.
A `threads` option on one machine; sharding across jobs is not documented in the fetched pages.

`--shard k/n` splits mutants across independent jobs, assigned by contiguous slice (the default) or round-robin with `--sharding`, with no coordination between shards; the page gives a GitHub Actions matrix example and says the CI system launches the shards and collects their results. Ours differs in partitioning by estimated cost rather than by count.

StrykerJS `--incremental` reuses results from reports/stryker-incremental.json and re-tests mutants in changed mutated or test files; the page says it will not detect changes in other files. Selection is of MUTANTS by file diff, not of suites by import closure.
Stryker.NET `since` (a git committish) mutates only source changed since it, and a changed test file marks the mutants it covers as changed; `with-baseline` is marked experimental.

Between runs it re-tests only mutants in functions whose source changed, and can be limited by name globs or `only_mutate`; a git-diff or import-closure selection is not documented in the fetched pages.

Experimental incremental analysis via history files reuses a result when the class under test and the killing test are unchanged, tracking only its strongest dependencies (superclasses, outer classes); import-closure selection of suites is not documented in the fetched pages.
That PIT's git-diff (scmMutationCoverage-style) selection now lives in the separate Arcmutate product: NOT fetched from Arcmutate's or PIT's own page, so unverified.
`--in-diff` tests only mutants overlapping changed regions of a diff and ignores test-code changes; the page says it is not a substitute for a full test run.
`--iterate` skips mutants caught in a previous run, described as a heuristic.

Pipeline use is break thresholds (an exit code) and a dashboard report upload (https://stryker-mutator.io/docs/General/dashboard/); a scheduled sweep or filing an issue is not documented in the fetched pages.
Offers `export-cicd-stats` and a badge; a scheduled sweep or filing an issue is not documented in the fetched pages.
A `mutationThreshold` fails the build; a scheduled sweep or filing an issue is not documented in the fetched pages.
Shows a full run on pushes to main and diff-only runs on PRs, with GitHub annotations; a cron schedule or filing an issue is not documented in the fetched pages.

conclusions: a: of the four, only cargo-mutants documents sharding one run across CI jobs (https://mutants.rs/shards.html); its assignment is by slice or round-robin, ours by estimated cost.

b: all four document selecting MUTANTS by what changed (file, function, class or diff region); none of the fetched pages documents selecting test suites by the import closure of a change, or by observed reads.
c: none of the fetched pages documents a scheduled full sweep that files an issue; cargo-mutants' full run on push to main (https://mutants.rs/ci.html) is the nearest.
